title: Admiral Makarov
summary: Admiral Makarov refers to various individuals and vessels, with significant connections to naval history and maritime education relevant to [[ukraine|Ukraine]].

sections.heading: Notable Individuals
paragraphs: Konstantin Makarov (1931–2011) was a Soviet Admiral of the Fleet, contributing to naval operations during the Soviet era.
Stepan Makarov (1849–1904) served as a Russian vice admiral and is recognized for his naval strategies and contributions to maritime warfare.

sections.heading: Naval Vessels
paragraphs: The Russian frigate Admiral Makarov was commissioned in 2017 and is part of the modern naval fleet, reflecting ongoing maritime developments in the region.
An icebreaker named Admiral Makarov was completed in 1975, playing a role in Arctic navigation and operations.
The Russian cruiser Admiral Makarov was in service from 1908 to 1922, representing a significant period in naval history.
The Soviet cruiser Admiral Makarov (1946) was formerly the German cruiser Nürnberg and was part of the Soviet naval fleet post-World War II.
Another Soviet cruiser, Admiral Makarov (1970), was a Kresta II-class cruiser that served from 1972 until 1992, during a pivotal time in the Cold War.
The vessel known as Admiral Makarov was originally the United States Coast Guard ship USCGC Southwind, which was lent to [[soviet-union|the Soviet Union]] from 1945 to 1949.
MV Admiral Makarov (1939) was a Soviet cargo liner that later became the research vessel Vityaz, contributing to maritime research.

sections.heading: Educational Institution
paragraphs: The Admiral Makarov State Maritime Academy is an educational institution that focuses on maritime studies and training, playing a crucial role in developing maritime professionals [[coal-in-ukraine|in Ukraine]].
